input.strategy_title: Idle resource reporting in the web console
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Cluster administrators cannot see which resources are sitting idle: workbenches
nobody has touched in weeks keep their volumes and reservations, and old
pipeline runs accumulate storage. Admins ask for a single report in the RHOAI
web console showing idle and stale resources per project so they can reclaim
capacity with confidence. The notebook controller already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata — the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Administrators can export either report as CSV. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. |

## Affected Components

- RHOAI web console
- Notebook controller
- Kubeflow Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources
- Cost/chargeback calculations

## Open Questions

None.

# Expose workbench last-activity on a Kubernetes-readable surface

## Description

Conditional epic, active only if the workbench-activity data-source
investigation resolves to the outcome where per-workbench last-activity data is
not readable through the Kubernetes API today. This epic makes the notebook
controller expose each workbench's last-activity timestamp on a
Kubernetes-readable surface (for example, the Notebook CR status) so the web
console's idle-workbench report can source it through the Kubernetes API
without private component APIs. The controller's existing activity tracking and
idle-culling behavior are preserved unchanged.

## Scope

- Notebook-controller changes that publish the already-tracked per-workbench
  last-activity value to a Kubernetes-readable surface, following the exposure
  path recommended by the completed data-source investigation.
- Population of the exposed value for all workbenches the controller
  reconciles, kept current as activity probes update it.
- Preservation of existing culling behavior: the idle culler, its
  configuration, and its decision logic are unchanged by this work.
- Out of scope: any console-side reporting work (the console report that
  consumes this surface is planned in the main plan), and any change to what
  the controller counts as activity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a running workbench with recorded activity, its last-activity value is
  readable through the Kubernetes API on the exposed surface, without private
  component APIs.
- The exposed value stays current as the workbench is used and goes idle.
- The idle culler's behavior is unchanged: culling decisions, defaults, and
  per-workbench overrides behave exactly as before the change (regression
  check).
- The console idle-workbench report can populate its last-activity column from
  the exposed surface.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)** — enables: supplies the Kubernetes-readable last-activity data
  source that the per-project idle-workbench report consumes, in the
  investigation outcome where no readable surface exists today.

# Workbench last-activity data source investigation for console reporting

## Description

This investigation determines how the notebook controller's per-workbench
last-activity tracking can be consumed by the RHOAI web console for the
per-project idle-workbench report. The console's only interface to component
backends is the Kubernetes API (no private component APIs), while the notebook
controller tracks last activity per kernel through Jupyter server API probes
driven by its culler. Whether that tracked value is readable today through a
Kubernetes-API surface (for example, a Notebook CR status field or an
equivalent readable resource) — or whether the controller must first expose it
— decides the shape of the downstream console reporting work and whether
notebook-controller code changes are needed at all.

## Scope

- Locate, in the notebook-controller source and configuration, where
  per-workbench last-activity timestamps are stored and updated (activity
  probes, culler config, any existing status or annotation writes).
- Determine whether that data is currently readable through the Kubernetes API
  by a console consumer, without private APIs or in-process access.
- Enumerate the viable consumption paths for a console report (existing
  readable surface, controller-side exposure of the value, or another
  Kubernetes-readable mechanism), assessing each against the console's
  Kubernetes-API-only interface constraint.
- Recommend one path, with a concrete pass/fail criterion the reporting
  implementation can test (a named field or surface to read).
- If the data is not readable today, specify what controller-side change would
  expose it and the impact on the console report's scope and sequencing.

## Outcomes

Two bounded outcomes:

- **Outcome A — the data is already readable via the Kubernetes API**: the
  console report reads the existing surface; no notebook-controller changes.
- **Outcome B — the data is not readable today**: notebook-controller work is
  required to expose per-workbench last-activity on a Kubernetes-readable
  surface; the conditional branch plan for that work is attached to this
  investigation's outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written findings report states, with source-level evidence, where
  per-workbench last-activity is stored and whether it is readable through the
  Kubernetes API today.
- Every candidate consumption path is assessed against the console's
  Kubernetes-API-only interface constraint, with the assessment recorded in the
  findings.
- The recommendation names a concrete, testable data source (field or surface)
  for the idle-workbench report, or — if none exists — the specific
  controller-side change required to create one.
- The outcome (A or B) is recorded so the reporting work and any conditional
  controller-side work can be scheduled from it.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)** — enables: resolves the data-source unknown behind the
  per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources)
  sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking.

# Console idle-workbench report with CSV export

## Description

This epic delivers the per-project idle-workbench report in the RHOAI web
console: an administrator-facing report showing, for each workbench in a
project, its last activity, owner, and reserved resources, sourced from the
notebook controller's activity tracking. It also delivers CSV export of the
report so administrators can export the data for offline use. Cluster
administrators use this report to see which workbenches are sitting idle and
reclaim capacity with confidence; no automated reclamation is performed.

## Scope

- A new administrator-facing report view in the web console, scoped per
  project, listing workbenches with their last activity, owner, and reserved
  resources.
- Data wiring that sources last-activity from the Kubernetes-readable surface
  identified by the completed workbench-activity data-source investigation; if
  that investigation found no readable surface, the wiring is built against the
  surface exposed by the conditional notebook-controller work once it lands.
- Read-only consumption of notebook-controller data through the Kubernetes API
  — no private component APIs, no changes to notebook-controller behavior (the
  idle culler and its configuration remain unaffected).
- A CSV export action on the report that downloads the currently displayed
  per-project idle-workbench data.
- Out of scope: automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources, and
  cost/chargeback calculations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project with workbenches, the console shows the idle-workbench report
  listing each workbench with its last activity, owner, and reserved resources.
- The report's last-activity data is populated from the notebook controller's
  activity tracking via the Kubernetes API, using the surface identified by the
  data-source investigation.
- Notebook-controller behavior is unchanged by this epic: the idle culler
  continues to operate with its existing configuration (passive-component
  validation).
- Administrators can export the idle-workbench report as CSV, and the exported
  file contains the report's rows and columns.
- The report is display-only: no reclamation or deletion action is offered.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)** — delivers the per-project idle-workbench report (last
  activity, owner, reserved resources) sourced from the notebook controller's
  activity tracking.
- **HLR-3 (P2, bundled)** — CSV export of the report is implemented here: the
  export action lives on this report's own UI surface and shares its data, so
  it is not separately schedulable from the report itself.

# Console stale pipeline-run report with CSV export

## Description

This epic delivers the per-project stale pipeline-run report in the RHOAI web
console: an administrator-facing report showing completed pipeline runs older
than a configurable age that still retain artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow
Pipelines run metadata (which the platform already retains and already surfaces
in the console). It also delivers CSV export of the report. Administrators use
this report to find old pipeline runs accumulating storage and reclaim capacity
with confidence; no automated reclamation is performed.

## Scope

- A new administrator-facing report view in the web console, scoped per
  project, listing completed pipeline runs older than a configurable age
  threshold, together with an indication of their retained artifacts.
- An administrator-configurable age threshold that controls which completed
  runs count as stale.
- Data wiring that sources run completion metadata through the console's
  existing Kubeflow Pipelines integration (KFP v2 run metadata) — read-only
  consumption, no changes to the Data Science Pipelines component, its
  operator, or its persistence.
- A CSV export action on the report that downloads the currently displayed
  per-project stale-run data.
- Out of scope: automated reclamation or deletion of runs or artifacts, and
  cost/chargeback calculations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project with completed pipeline runs, the console shows the stale
  pipeline-run report listing completed runs older than the configured age,
  with their retained artifacts indicated.
- The age threshold is configurable, and changing it changes which runs the
  report lists.
- The report's data is populated from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata via the
  console's existing pipelines integration.
- The Data Science Pipelines component is unchanged by this epic: run
  execution, metadata retention, and artifact storage behave exactly as before
  (passive-component validation).
- Administrators can export the stale pipeline-run report as CSV, and the
  exported file contains the report's rows and columns.
- The report is display-only: no reclamation or deletion action is offered.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1)** — delivers the stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older
  than a configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow
  Pipelines run metadata.
- **HLR-3 (P2, bundled)** — CSV export of the report is implemented here: the
  export action lives on this report's own UI surface and shares its data, so
  it is not separately schedulable from the report itself.

# Documentation for the idle resource reports and safe reclamation steps

## Description

This epic delivers Red Hat documentation explaining the two new console reports
— the per-project idle-workbench report and the stale pipeline-run report — and
the steps administrators can take to safely reclaim the capacity those reports
surface. It is authored through the Red Hat docs content process after the
reports are implemented, so the documentation describes what was actually
built.

## Scope

- New documentation topics explaining both console reports and safe manual
  reclamation, covering:
  - What each report shows (columns: last activity, owner, reserved resources
    for workbenches; completed-run age and retained artifacts for pipeline
    runs) and where to find it in the web console.
  - How to configure the stale pipeline-run age threshold.
  - How to interpret the reports to identify idle workbenches and stale
    pipeline runs.
  - Safe reclamation steps for each resource type, including cautions about
    data that may be lost and the explicit statement that reclamation is
    manual (the platform does not automatically reclaim or delete resources).
  - What is intentionally not covered: automated reclamation and
    cost/chargeback.
- Accuracy validation of every documented claim against the shipped reports
  and against the platform architecture context (console interfaces,
  notebook-controller activity tracking, Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata).
- Screenshots and captions that fall out of the documented flows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation explains both reports: what they show, where in the
  console they appear, and how to read their columns.
- Published documentation explains how to configure the stale pipeline-run age
  threshold.
- Published documentation includes safe reclamation steps for idle workbenches
  and stale pipeline runs, and clearly states that reclamation is manual.
- The documentation has been technically reviewed against the implemented
  reports (reviewed by the implementing engineers) and validated against the
  platform architecture context before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — delivers documentation explaining the reports and safe
  reclamation steps.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9016: Idle resource reporting in the web console

Strategy status: Refinement Done. Strategy priority: Normal.

Triage: neither Step 0 check fires. The strategy is not below threshold — it
spans three affected components and at least two owning teams, and it contains
multiple distinct work streams (two console report implementations over
different backend data sources, plus substantive documentation authoring). It
is not documentation-only. Full decomposition follows.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 | Workbench last-activity data source investigation for console reporting | Investigation | Workbenches | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E002 | Console idle-workbench report with CSV export | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E003 | Console stale pipeline-run report with CSV export | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E004 | Documentation for the idle resource reports and safe reclamation steps | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Dashboard | P2 |
| RHAISTRAT-9016-BRANCH-B-E005 | Expose workbench last-activity on a Kubernetes-readable surface (conditional, outcome B only) | Implementation | Workbenches | P1 |

Main plan: E001–E004. BRANCH-B-E005 is a conditional branch epic attached to
the E001 investigation outcome; it is not a main-plan node.

## Component Mapping

Strategy component names → canonical RHAI Jira components
(`.context/rhai-components.txt`), with active/passive classification:

| Strategy component | Canonical component | Owner team | Classification |
|--------------------|----------------------|------------|----------------|
| RHOAI web console | Dashboard | RHOAI Dashboard | Active — both reports are built here |
| Notebook controller | Notebooks | Workbenches | Passive in outcome A (activity already tracked, no code change); active in branch B (exposure work needed) |
| Kubeflow Pipelines | Data Science Pipelines | RHOAI Pipelines | Passive — run completion metadata is already retained and pipeline runs are already surfaced in the console (data-science-pipelines.md); read-only consumption, validated as an acceptance criterion on E003. No separate validation epic: the consuming team (RHOAI Dashboard) is the validator. |

The documentation epic uses the canonical `Documentation` component. Team
ownership for it is an assumption (see Health Warnings) — the strategy names no
doc owner, so it is assigned to the console team whose feature is documented.

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 Investigation: workbench activity data source"] --> E002["E002 Idle-workbench report + CSV"]
    E002 --> E004["E004 Documentation"]
    E003["E003 Stale pipeline-run report + CSV"] --> E004
    E001 -. "outcome B only (conditional)" .-> BE005["BRANCH-B-E005 Expose last-activity (branch epic)"]
```

Arrows point from dependency to dependent. The dashed edge is a conditional
gate, not a main-plan edge: BRANCH-B-E005 exists only if the investigation
resolves to outcome B, and no main-plan epic depends on it.

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 3 (Investigation edges) | Whether the notebook controller's last-activity data is readable through the Kubernetes API today determines how the report's data wiring is built and whether controller-side exposure work exists. Bounded to two outcomes → conditional branch (below), not phased decomposition. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation describes the built reports; must follow all Implementation epics. |
| E003 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Same. |
| E001 ⇢ BRANCH-B-E005 | Rule 3 / conditional decomposition | The branch epic is gated by the investigation and exists only in outcome B. |
| E003 has no dependencies | Rules 14/15 | KFP run metadata is already retained and pipeline runs are already surfaced in the console (data-science-pipelines.md corroborates); no gating unknown, no shared artifact under construction. Starts immediately, in parallel with E001. |

Boundary decisions:

- **E002 and E003 are separate epics** despite sharing component and team: they
  are separate report surfaces over architecturally distinct data sources
  (Notebook CR activity data vs. Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata), and only E002
  is gated by the investigation. Splitting along the data-source boundary keeps
  the ungated pipeline-run report from being serialized behind the workbench
  unknown.
